name: Logical order of SQL clause evaluation
notes: Knowing it means being able to say why a SELECT alias can't be used in WHERE, and why WHERE and HAVING are not interchangeable.

name: Join types and what each keeps
notes: Knowing it means stating, for each join, which side's unmatched rows survive and what their missing columns become.

name: Row multiplication from a non-unique join key
notes: Knowing it means being able to describe how a one-to-many join inflates a SUM, and how you'd check for it before trusting the number.

name: NULL is not a value
notes: Knowing it means explaining three-valued logic: why NULL = NULL isn't true, why NOT IN with a NULL returns nothing, and why COUNT(*) and COUNT(col) differ.

name: GROUP BY grain and HAVING
notes: Knowing it means saying that the GROUP BY list defines the output grain, and that HAVING filters groups while WHERE filters rows.

name: CTEs, subqueries, and materialization
notes: Knowing it means saying that readability is the main win, and that whether a CTE is inlined or materialized is engine-dependent and can flip performance.

name: CASE expressions and conditional aggregation
notes: Knowing it means writing SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as a pivot, and spotting the missing ELSE that turns zeros into NULLs.

name: Window functions vs aggregates
notes: Knowing it means saying in one sentence that a window computes per row without collapsing the grain, which is the whole idea.

name: PARTITION BY
notes: Knowing it means explaining that PARTITION BY resets the window per group — same grouping intent as GROUP BY, different output grain.

name: Window frame clause
notes: Knowing it means being able to say why RANGE and ROWS differ when there are ties, and that the default frame with ORDER BY is RANGE, not ROWS.

name: ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK
notes: Knowing it means describing tie and gap behavior for each, and saying that deduplication almost always wants ROW_NUMBER.

name: Date truncation, boundaries, and time zones
notes: Knowing it means preferring half-open intervals, spotting that BETWEEN on timestamps drops the last day, and storing UTC while displaying local.

name: What an index actually is
notes: Knowing it means describing an index as a sorted structure trading write cost and storage for read speed, and why one on a low-cardinality column often does nothing.

name: Reading an EXPLAIN plan
notes: Knowing it means reading inside-out and looking first at the gap between estimated and actual rows, because that is where the trouble usually is.

name: Sargable predicates
notes: Knowing it means seeing that wrapping an indexed column in a function kills the index, and rewriting DATE(ts) = x as a range on ts.

name: Shuffles, spills, and skew
notes: Knowing it means explaining that distributed joins move data between nodes, and that one hot key can leave a single worker doing all the work.

name: Partition pruning
notes: Knowing it means naming the filter that lets the engine skip whole files, and recognizing its absence as the difference between seconds and minutes.

name: The real cost of SELECT *
notes: Knowing it means framing it as scan volume in a columnar store plus a schema-drift hazard downstream, not as a style preference.

name: Reasoning about query cost before running it
notes: Knowing it means estimating bytes scanned from partitions and columns touched, and knowing which knob actually moves the bill.

name: Normalization and what it buys
notes: Knowing it means stating the one-fact-in-one-place principle and naming an update anomaly that normalization prevents.

name: Deliberate denormalization
notes: Knowing it means trading write complexity for read speed on purpose, and saying what you owe in return: a rebuild path and a consistency story.

name: Star schema
notes: Knowing it means saying facts measure and dimensions describe, and why that shape is legible to both BI tools and business users.

name: Declaring the grain of a fact table
notes: Knowing it means finishing the sentence 'one row per ___' before writing any DDL, and explaining what breaks when the grain is fudged.

name: Transaction, periodic snapshot, accumulating snapshot
notes: Knowing it means picking the right one for a given question, and explaining why a balance is not a transaction.

name: Additive, semi-additive, and non-additive measures
notes: Knowing it means explaining why summing a rate or a balance across time is nonsense, and what to do with each instead.

name: Dimension tables and conformed dimensions
notes: Knowing it means arguing that shared dimensions are what make two marts comparable, which is why 'one customer table' is a fight worth having.

name: Slowly changing dimensions, type 1 vs type 2
notes: Knowing it means describing valid_from, valid_to and a current flag, and naming a case where simply overwriting is the right call.

name: Surrogate vs natural keys
notes: Knowing it means saying surrogates decouple you from source-system key churn, and that SCD2 cannot work without them.

name: The semantic layer
notes: Knowing it means arguing for one definition of a metric reused everywhere, because the alternative is nine dashboards with nine revenues.

name: One big table vs star schema
notes: Knowing it means acknowledging columnar engines made OBT viable, and naming what you give up: reuse, governance, and a shared dimension definition.

name: OLAP vs OLTP
notes: Knowing it means deriving the storage, indexing and normalization differences from the access pattern, not just saying 'analytics vs app'.

name: Columnar storage
notes: Knowing it means saying you read only the columns you ask for and compress well because neighbors are alike — which explains most warehouse performance advice.

name: Separation of storage and compute
notes: Knowing it means explaining why modern warehouses bill per query-second while idle storage stays cheap.

name: Parquet, and why not CSV
notes: Knowing it means naming typed, columnar, compressed, and per-row-group statistics that enable predicate pushdown.

name: Table formats and the lakehouse
notes: Knowing it means describing Iceberg or Delta as a metadata layer giving files ACID, schema evolution and time travel — what makes a lake behave like a table.

name: Views vs materialized views
notes: Knowing it means saying a view is saved SQL and a materialized view is saved results plus a staleness problem you now own.

name: ETL vs ELT
notes: Knowing it means explaining that cheap warehouse compute moved the T after the L, and what that changes about debugging and reprocessing.

name: Idempotent pipeline runs
notes: Knowing it means defining it as running twice equals running once, and explaining why it is what makes retries safe and on-call survivable.

name: At-least-once, at-most-once, exactly-once
notes: Knowing it means saying most systems give at-least-once, and that exactly-once is usually at-least-once plus a dedupe key.

name: Incremental loads
notes: Knowing it means naming the change signal you rely on and a merge strategy that survives a replay of the same window.

name: Change data capture
notes: Knowing it means contrasting log-based with query-based CDC, and saying log-based catches deletes and does not hammer the source.

name: Late-arriving data and watermarks
notes: Knowing it means separating event time from processing time, and saying that how long you hold a window open is a business decision.

name: Batch vs streaming
notes: Knowing it means driving the choice off the real latency requirement, which is almost always looser than first claimed.

name: dbt materializations
notes: Knowing it means choosing between view, table, incremental and ephemeral by the cost and freshness tradeoff each makes.

name: dbt tests and the ref graph
notes: Knowing it means treating unique, not_null, relationships and accepted_values as a cheap contract, and knowing ref() is what builds the DAG.

name: DAGs and orchestration
notes: Knowing it means saying dependencies rather than clock times are the primitive, and why 'run at 3am and hope' is not orchestration.

name: Asset-oriented vs task-oriented orchestration
notes: Knowing it means describing the shift from "run this step" to "this table should exist", and what it buys you at debug time.

name: Backfills
notes: Knowing it means reprocessing history a partition at a time without corrupting the present or saturating the warehouse.

name: Retries, timeouts, and what deserves a page
notes: Knowing it means pairing retry policy with idempotency, and distinguishing a failure that can wait until morning from one that can't.

name: Failure blast radius in a DAG
notes: Knowing it means choosing deliberately what downstream does when upstream fails: fail, skip, or serve stale — and defending the choice.

name: Data contracts
notes: Knowing it means describing an agreement with the producer over schema, semantics and notice period — a social artifact with technical teeth.

name: Freshness checks
notes: Knowing it means naming the pipeline that succeeds while producing nothing new as the most dangerous failure mode there is.

name: Schema drift
notes: Knowing it means describing how a silently renamed upstream column reaches a dashboard, and how you'd catch it before a stakeholder does.

name: Row-count and distribution anomalies
notes: Knowing it means preferring relative-to-history over fixed thresholds, and explaining why a static row-count alarm gets muted within a month.

name: Null-rate monitoring
notes: Knowing it means reading a jump from 2% to 40% null as a broken join upstream rather than a quirk of the data.

name: Reconciling against the source of truth
notes: Knowing it means answering 'does my number match finance's number' and having the discipline to write down why it doesn't.

name: Alert fatigue in data quality
notes: Knowing it means arguing that an alert nobody acts on is worse than no alert, because it teaches the team to ignore the channel.

name: Defining a metric precisely
notes: Knowing it means specifying numerator, denominator, population, window and exclusions, and recognizing most 'discrepancies' as definition disputes.

name: Survivorship and selection bias
notes: Knowing it means asking who is missing from the table, and what their absence does to the average.

name: Cohort analysis
notes: Knowing it means grouping by entry period and measuring across relative time, which separates 'we changed' from 'the mix changed'.

name: Simpson's paradox
notes: Knowing it means explaining how a trend present in every segment can reverse in aggregate, and why 'check the mix' is a standing rule.

name: Correlation vs causation
notes: Knowing it means naming confounders, reverse causation and coincidence — and saying so to a stakeholder without sounding obstructive.

name: Averages hide distributions
notes: Knowing it means reaching for medians and percentiles, and identifying a case where the mean is actively misleading.

name: Statistical significance and sample size
notes: Knowing it means explaining a confidence interval in plain language, and what 'not significant' does and does not mean.

name: A/B test fundamentals
notes: Knowing it means naming the randomization unit, the cost of peeking, multiple comparisons, and pre-registering the metric.

name: Choosing an encoding for the question
notes: Knowing it means mapping comparison, composition, distribution, relationship and trend to a chart form, so the question picks the chart.

name: Axis truncation and scale honesty
notes: Knowing it means requiring a zero baseline for bars but not always for lines, and saying when truncation is clarity and when it's deception.

name: Dashboard information hierarchy
notes: Knowing it means putting one question per screen with the headline first and detail on demand, and seeing a 20-tile dashboard as answering nothing.

name: Big-O and when it actually matters
notes: Knowing it means talking about growth rate rather than speed, and recognizing the O(n^2) that's fine at 200 rows and fatal at 200,000.

name: Hash maps and constant-time lookup
notes: Knowing it means explaining hashing, buckets and collisions — the model behind a dict, a set, and a hash join.

name: Choosing a data structure
notes: Knowing it means spotting membership tests against a list as the single highest-leverage fix in most slow scripts.

name: Mutability and aliasing
notes: Knowing it means explaining two names for one object, and predicting the mutable-default-argument bug before it happens.

name: Concurrency vs parallelism
notes: Knowing it means distinguishing interleaving from simultaneity, and matching I/O-bound work to threads and CPU-bound work to processes.

name: Race conditions and shared state
notes: Knowing it means describing a read-modify-write interleaving that loses an update, and naming the cheapest fix that actually works.

name: Generators and lazy evaluation
notes: Knowing it means producing one item at a time instead of materializing a list, and saying what that fixes in memory and costs in reuse.

name: Context managers
notes: Knowing it means explaining guaranteed cleanup on exception, so `with open(...)` is correctness rather than style.

name: Exception handling strategy
notes: Knowing it means catching narrowly at the layer that can act, and explaining why a bare except is a bug incubator.

name: Virtual environments and dependency pinning
notes: Knowing it means isolating per project and pinning with a lockfile, and framing 'works on my machine' as a dependency story.

name: Vectorized operations vs row loops
notes: Knowing it means recognizing iterrows as the default performance mistake and pushing work into the library's compiled loop.

name: The GIL
notes: Knowing it means saying why threads help an I/O-bound extract but not a CPU-bound transform, and what to reach for instead.

name: Git's object model in plain terms
notes: Knowing it means describing commits as snapshots with parents and branches as movable pointers — the model that resolves most git confusion.

name: Rebase vs merge
notes: Knowing it means contrasting rewriting history with recording it, and explaining why you don't rebase a shared branch.

name: Commit granularity and messages
notes: Knowing it means one logical change per commit, with the message explaining why since the diff already shows what.

name: Recovering from a bad git state
notes: Knowing it means reaching for reflog, and saying which of revert and reset is actually destructive and to whom.

name: Unit, integration, and end-to-end tests
notes: Knowing it means saying what each level catches and costs, and why an all-E2E suite becomes a flaky tax.

name: Where to mock
notes: Knowing it means mocking at the system boundary, and recognizing an over-mocked test as asserting your assumptions back at you.

name: Choosing what deserves a test
notes: Knowing it means targeting branching logic and boundaries — testing a getter proves nothing, testing an SM-2 threshold proves a lot.

name: Pure functions and testability
notes: Knowing it means defining same-input-same-output with no side effects, and why the scheduling module is pure while storage is not.

name: Turning a bug into a test
notes: Knowing it means writing the failing test first, so the fix is proven and the bug can't quietly return.

name: Systematic debugging
notes: Knowing it means reproducing, bisecting, and testing one hypothesis at a time — and reading the actual error before theorizing.

name: Logging levels and what to log
notes: Knowing it means logging enough context to diagnose without a rerun, and never logging secrets or full personal-data payloads.

name: Fail fast vs degrade gracefully
notes: Knowing it means arguing that a partially-loaded table is worse than a failed job, and identifying which failures must be loud.

name: Separating config from code
notes: Knowing it means keeping environment-specific values outside the source, which is what lets one artifact run in dev and prod.

name: Refactoring behind a test
notes: Knowing it means changing structure without changing behavior, which is only meaningful once behavior is pinned.

name: Premature abstraction
notes: Knowing it means arguing that duplication is cheaper than the wrong abstraction, and waiting for the third instance.

name: Giving and taking a code review
notes: Knowing it means separating correctness from clarity from taste, and labeling which one you're raising.

name: HTTP verbs and resource shape
notes: Knowing it means saying what each verb implies about safety and repeatability, not just which one you happened to use.

name: Status codes that matter
notes: Knowing it means separating 4xx you caused from 5xx they caused, and distinguishing 401 from 403 and 429 from both.

name: Pagination strategies
notes: Knowing it means contrasting offset with cursor, and explaining how offset pagination silently skips rows on changing data.

name: API keys, bearer tokens, and OAuth
notes: Knowing it means saying who the credential identifies, where it may be stored, and what rotating it involves.

name: Rate limits and backoff
notes: Knowing it means using exponential backoff with jitter, and explaining why a flat one-second sleep creates a thundering herd.

name: How static hosting works
notes: Knowing it means saying files are served as-is with no server process, which is why it's free and why it can't keep a secret.

name: The DOM and event handling
notes: Knowing it means describing a tree you query and mutate, with events bubbling up it — the basis of every interaction in the app.

name: Promises, async/await, and the event loop
notes: Knowing it means explaining single-threaded but non-blocking, and why a forgotten await hands you a Promise instead of data.

name: fetch and loading JSON on demand
notes: Knowing it means loading a per-domain bank file at run time and handling a failed fetch without a blank screen.

name: CORS and same-origin policy
notes: Knowing it means explaining why the browser blocks a cross-origin fetch and what headers the Worker must return in phase 2.

name: Flexbox and grid
notes: Knowing it means choosing one-dimensional versus two-dimensional layout — enough to build a card, a pip row and a stacked session view.

name: Keyboard focus and semantic HTML
notes: Knowing it means using real buttons and labels with visible focus, which is also the fastest path to a keyboard-driven drill.

name: Why a client-side app can't hold an API key
notes: Knowing it means stating that anything shipped to the browser is public, which is the entire reason model grading needs a proxy.

name: localStorage: shape, limits, and failure modes
notes: Knowing it means saying synchronous, string-only, per-origin, roughly 5MB, and able to throw in private mode — so wrap every read and write.

name: JSON serialization round-trips
notes: Knowing it means predicting that Dates become strings, undefined disappears and Maps don't survive — which the export format must tolerate.

name: Versioning persisted state
notes: Knowing it means shipping a version field plus a migration path so a schema change doesn't orphan months of progress.

name: Manual export and import as sync
notes: Knowing it means accepting replace-not-merge as the honest stopgap for three devices, and naming the divergence it can't solve.

name: The spacing effect and retrieval practice
notes: Knowing it means explaining why effortful recall at increasing intervals beats rereading — the premise the whole app rests on.

name: SM-2 in its essentials
notes: Knowing it means describing interval, repetition count and ease factor, and the 1/6/interval*ease progression, in about forty lines.

name: Ease factor and the 1.8 floor
notes: Knowing it means explaining that without a floor a few bad nights drive an item into permanent daily punishment — a design decision, not a tweak.

name: Mapping rubric ratio to SM-2 quality
notes: Knowing it means reciting the thresholds — 0.8 to q5, 0.6 to q4, 0.4 to q3, below that a lapse — and why every boundary is unit-tested.

name: Scheduling concepts, not questions
notes: Knowing it means arguing that many question types are views of one memory, so per-question state multiplies review load for no learning gain.

name: Choosing a question type at presentation time
notes: Knowing it means picking a rendering not recently shown for that concept, so variety comes from the bank rather than the schedule.

name: Reserving a slot for new material
notes: Knowing it means explaining that strict priority starves new concepts permanently once due volume reaches the cap, and reserved slots fix it.

name: The forgetting rule
notes: Knowing it means dropping anything over 60 days overdue back to new, and explaining how a long absence compounds without it.

name: The Return Path
notes: Knowing it means making a return after three weeks feel like a normal night: surface a few, silently redistribute the rest, never show a count.

name: Scheduling from answer time, not grade time
notes: Knowing it means seeing that if grading lands later, keying intervals off the grade collapses several offline nights into one date.

name: Keeping extra reps out of the schedule
notes: Knowing it means logging beyond-the-cap reps without updating intervals, so a 40-question binge does not build a backlog three days later.

name: Bounded sessions and the hard stop
notes: Knowing it means defending four questions, discrete pips and a terminal screen as what makes the app survivable on a bad day.

name: No streaks, no loss states, no backlog count
notes: Knowing it means arguing that streaks punish the return, and that the design goal is a frictionless resume rather than compliance.

name: Zero decisions before the first question
notes: Knowing it means cutting the home screen entirely, because every pre-session choice is a place to bounce off.

name: Capture without a chore
notes: Knowing it means a two-second paste box with no metadata fields, because anything slower stops getting used within a week.

name: Offline-first as a constraint
notes: Knowing it means naming what offline-first rules out and what it makes free, rather than treating it as a nice-to-have.

name: Writing a checkable rubric criterion
notes: Knowing it means writing concrete booleans — 'names the fanout risk' beats 'shows good understanding' — because vague criteria make self-grading meaningless.

name: Why checklists beat numeric scores
notes: Knowing it means explaining that a model scores the same answer 70 one night and 85 the next, and that noticing costs you trust in the app.

name: Version-controlling prompts
notes: Knowing it means treating a prompt as source, so a regenerated question bank is reproducible and drift is visible in a diff.

name: Calibration fixtures for grading drift
notes: Knowing it means keeping ~20 fixture answers with expected results, because persisting questions guards generation drift but not grading drift.

name: Why reviewing feels like understanding
notes: Knowing it means articulating the recognition-versus-production gap that motivates this entire app.

name: Filesystem layout and paths
notes: Knowing it means navigating absolute versus relative paths and knowing where to look first on an unfamiliar box.

name: Unix permissions and ownership
notes: Knowing it means reading a permission string aloud and explaining why chmod 777 is a confession rather than a fix.

name: Processes, signals, and exit codes
notes: Knowing it means distinguishing SIGTERM from SIGKILL and treating any non-zero exit code as failure.

name: SSH key authentication
notes: Knowing it means public key on the server, private key never leaving your machine, and why key file permissions must be tight.

name: cron and scheduled jobs
notes: Knowing it means reading the five fields and anticipating the classic failure: a different environment and PATH than your shell.

name: systemd services
notes: Knowing it means setting a restart policy, reading journalctl, and knowing what it takes to survive a reboot.

name: Image vs container
notes: Knowing it means separating the template from the running instance, which makes every other Docker question tractable.

name: Dockerfile layers and build cache
notes: Knowing it means ordering instructions so dependencies install before source is copied, or the cache is thrown away every build.

name: Volumes and persistence
notes: Knowing it means treating containers as disposable and data as not, and saying where the database files actually live.

name: Compose as declarative local infrastructure
notes: Knowing it means describing the whole stack in one file, with the test being whether a fresh clone comes up clean.

name: Memory limits and the OOM kill
notes: Knowing it means recognizing a container killed with nothing in its own logs, and knowing where the real evidence is.

name: DNS records and propagation
notes: Knowing it means telling A from CNAME from TXT, and explaining TTL when a domain change 'isn't working yet'.

name: Ports, binding, and listening
notes: Knowing it means one listener per port, the difference between 0.0.0.0 and 127.0.0.1, and what 'address already in use' means.

name: HTTPS and what TLS actually guarantees
notes: Knowing it means saying it gives encryption in transit plus server identity, and nothing at all about the site being trustworthy.

name: Reverse proxies
notes: Knowing it means one public entrypoint terminating TLS and routing to internal services — the shape of a home server done properly.

name: Handling secrets
notes: Knowing it means environment variables or a secret store, never the repo — and knowing the first move when one is committed is rotation.

name: Least privilege
notes: Knowing it means giving a dashboard a read-only role, and framing the blast radius of a leaked credential as a design choice.

name: Backups are restores
notes: Knowing it means calling an untested backup a rumor, and describing what a real restore drill looks like and how long it takes.

name: Monitoring vs alerting
notes: Knowing it means saying everything is worth measuring and almost nothing is worth waking someone for.

name: Logs, metrics, and traces
notes: Knowing it means matching each to a question: metrics say whether it was slow, traces say where, logs say what happened.

name: Triaging an incident
notes: Knowing it means stopping the bleeding before finding the cause, and stating impact before theory.

name: Blameless postmortems
notes: Knowing it means producing a timeline, contributing factors and one concrete change — treating human error as a starting point, not a root cause.

name: Thinking in failure modes
notes: Knowing it means asking what breaks first under load, bad input or a dead dependency, before it does.

name: Calibrating to the audience
notes: Knowing it means identifying what they already know, what they'll do with this, and what they're actually worried about.

name: Answer first, then the reasoning
notes: Knowing it means leading with the conclusion, because building to it works in writing you control and fails in a meeting you don't.

name: The question behind the question
notes: Knowing it means hearing 'can I get last month's numbers' as a decision about to be made, and asking which one.

name: Explaining a technical concept to a non-technical audience
notes: Knowing it means one analogy, one concrete example, no smuggled jargon — and checking understanding without condescending.

name: Naming the tradeoff explicitly
notes: Knowing it means stating what a recommendation gives up, out loud, which is what makes the recommendation credible.

name: Recommending rather than presenting options
notes: Knowing it means leading with your pick and why, then the alternatives, because a neutral menu pushes your job onto the reader.

name: Surfacing assumptions
notes: Knowing it means stating what you assumed and proceeding, because silent assumptions are how two people agree and build different things.

name: Communicating uncertainty without hedging into mush
notes: Knowing it means giving a range and a confidence rather than a disclaimer paragraph — 'directionally right, not exact to the dollar'.

name: When the data contradicts a strongly held belief
notes: Knowing it means checking your own work first, then presenting it as a question rather than a verdict.

name: Delivering bad news early
notes: Knowing it means recognizing that the cost of a slip compounds with the delay in reporting it, and bringing options alongside the news.

name: Translating a metric into a decision
notes: Knowing it means saying 'conversion is down 4%' isn't an insight until it names what someone should do differently.

name: Data request intake
notes: Knowing it means asking for the decision, the deadline, the grain and the definition — four questions that prevent most rework.

name: Eliciting requirements from a vague ask
notes: Knowing it means showing a rough version early, because people recognize what they want faster than they can specify it.

name: Cutting scope and saying so
notes: Knowing it means offering 'here's what I'd drop and what that costs you' instead of a silent slip or a heroic weekend.

name: Pushing back constructively
notes: Knowing it means saying no to the request and yes to the underlying need, while naming the tradeoff you're protecting.

name: Two stakeholders, one you
notes: Knowing it means making the conflict visible to both rather than absorbing it silently, and treating escalation as a service.

name: Estimating with ranges
notes: Knowing it means giving a range plus the assumption that would blow it, since a single-point estimate gets heard as a commitment.

name: Defining done before starting
notes: Knowing it means agreeing what exists at the end, who checks it, and what would make it wrong — which prevents infinite revision.

name: Knowing who actually decides
notes: Knowing it means separating the requester, the decision-maker and the person who will be blamed — often three different people.

name: Status updates people actually read
notes: Knowing it means done, next, blocked — with consistency of cadence mattering more than length.

name: Writing a design doc
notes: Knowing it means stating the problem, the options considered, the choice and its consequences — so a reader can disagree specifically.

name: Communicating during an incident
notes: Knowing it means saying what's broken, who's affected, what you're doing and when you'll update next — then updating on schedule.

name: Closing the loop
notes: Knowing it means telling people it shipped and what changed — the cheapest reputation-building act available.

name: Describing your own work credibly
notes: Knowing it means situation, action, result with specific numbers — no inflation, and no shrinking either.
